summary: Define an auxiliary relation on names, prove its truth lemma, and recover ordinary semantic forcing and its formula-by-formula definability.
abstract: A condition forces a statement when that statement holds in every generic extension containing the condition. This meaning quantifies over filters outside the ground model, yet the forcing theorem lets the ground model recognize forcing by an ordinary set-theoretic formula. A recursive auxiliary relation on names makes this possible: its witnesses match the truth of membership, inequality and quantified formulas after names are evaluated. Translating the ordinary membership language and taking an auxiliary double negation recovers semantic forcing. The resulting truth lemma says that every true statement in a generic extension is already guaranteed by some condition of its generic filter; definability is a separate assertion for each fixed formula.
